person: Hana Kowalczyk is 34 and runs a one-person shop from a studio behind her house in Oregon, selling ceramics and linen goods (tea towels, aprons, napkins) on her own site and two marketplaces. She does everything herself and has never filed a takedown before; official forms and legal wording make her nervous. She has noticed copies of her linen photos and what looks like a knock-off of her apron on other sellers' listings and has a list of thirteen she screenshotted. She wants it sorted without having to dig through reports, and wants to know quickly if this is even a chore for a shop her size.
stated_up_front: Hi! I found a bunch of listings on Stallwick and Hawkerbrook that look like they're copying my linen photos, and a couple of aprons that look like fakes of mine. Can you go through my list and only go after the ones that are really ripping me off? I have orders to pack so keep the questions short please.

facts.about: Brand name and what she sells in linen
facts.truth: Her brand is 'Kowalczyk Linen Studio'; she sells tea towels, napkins and aprons in flax linen.

facts.about: Number of suspect listings she logged
facts.truth: Thirteen, collected in her sheet over about three weeks in September and October 2026.
She took the product photos herself in her studio, except one lifestyle shot of a napkin set that a customer, Dana, sent her; she does not own that one.
A boutique called Fernhill Home carries her tea towels under a wholesale deal and uses her photos with her permission.
She let a shop called Cedar & Thread use her photos for a spring promo; she told them it ended at the end of June 2026 and they are still using them.
She registered her brand name as a trademark with the US trademark office last year; the registration paperwork is in her Drive folder.
She bought two apron knock-offs herself in September, one from each marketplace, for about $24 each, and saved the receipts and photos of the stitching and tags.
One seller is reselling her real tea towels, bought from her wholesale at an invoice from March 2026, and using their own photos.
Two listings just say 'Kowalczyk Linen style' or 'like Kowalczyk Linen' in the title but show different goods and photos.
One Stallwick listing she logged earlier has already come down; it shows 'no longer available' when she clicks it.
One suspect listing is on a small site called Bazaarly where she has no seller account.
She sells about 40 to 60 orders a month, mostly $20 to $45 each.

unknowns: Whether a copyright notice or a trademark complaint is the right kind for each listing
What the law says about reselling genuine goods or about a licence that has ended
How long each marketplace takes to act after a notice is filed
What happens to her own seller account if a seller disputes a notice
